name: Chronic Hiccup

criteria.description: Hiccups persisting continuously for more than 48 hours
Exclusion of metabolic, central nervous system, and gastrointestinal causes
Repetitive, involuntary, spasmodic contractions of the diaphragm and intercostal muscles producing characteristic 'hic' sound
Poor or no response to standard transient hiccup treatments

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hiccups lasting more than 48 hours with exclusion of secondary causes and characteristic clinical features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of underlying systemic or neurological disorders.

searchTerms: defect or malformation of diaphragm muscle

laboratory: Normal metabolic panel unless secondary cause identified
Possible electrolyte abnormalities if prolonged vomiting occurs
imaging: Chest X-ray to exclude thoracic pathology
Brain MRI if central nervous system cause suspected
Upper GI endoscopy if reflux or esophageal pathology suspected
other: Response to diagnostic nerve blocks may aid in localization

distinguishingFeatures: Associated symptoms such as headache or focal weakness
Absence of persistent hiccups beyond transient episodes

redFlags: Onset of hiccups associated with neurological symptoms
Hiccups lasting longer than 1 month without improvement
Signs of systemic illness such as fever, weight loss, or night sweats
references: Kahrilas PJ, et al. Chronic hiccups: pathophysiology and treatment. Gastroenterology. 2020.
Steger M, Schneemann M. Persistent and intractable hiccup: an overview. J Clin Gastroenterol. 2019.
